newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Friday with most investors remaining on the sidelines ahead of the weekend, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,408 yuan ($411) per tonne, unchanged from Thursday's close. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,371 and hit a high of 3,418.
May rose five yuan to 3,365, September fell three yuan to 3,444 and November five to 3,445. The January 1998 contract put on 10 to 3,440.
Combined volume rose slightly to 15,300 tonnes from 13,700.
Soybeans opened lower and short-covering pushed prices off lows for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the weekend, which resulted in slow trading," one trader said. "But soybeans have strong support at low levels due to improved fundamentals."
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue to move around the current level early next week.
